questions.text: What are Custom Agents in Kiro?

options.label: Specialized Markdown profiles that combine a system prompt, tools, MCP servers, and permission rules
Temporary subprocesses automatically created by the main agent for every tool call
Steering files with `auto` inclusion, renamed when they declare their own tools
Scheduled automations that run a prompt in a sandbox without the user selecting an agent

questions.explanation: A Custom Agent is defined in Markdown with YAML front matter. The configuration can select tools, MCP servers, and permission rules, while the file body acts as its specialized system prompt.

questions.text: Workspace Custom Agents are available only when the workspace is trusted.

options.label: True
False

questions.explanation: True. Kiro only loads workspace agents in trusted workspaces because those files can grant tools, commands, and MCP servers. Global agents live in `~/.kiro/agents/`.

questions.text: Where are Custom Agents configured in a Kiro project?

options.label: In the editor's settings.json file
In the .kiro/agents/ directory of the project, in configuration files
In the Kiro global preferences panel
In the project's package.json file, in the 'kiro' section

questions.explanation: Custom Agents are configured in the .kiro/agents/ directory of the project. Each agent has its own configuration file that defines its system prompt, available tools, and scope of action.

questions.text: Your team switches between a React frontend and a Python backend and wants selectable profiles with different tools and instructions. How should this be configured?

options.label: Increase the context token limit in settings
Create two Custom Agents in `.kiro/agents/`, each with a prompt, tools, and MCP servers suited to its domain
Manually switch between different projects in the editor
Use .kiroignore to hide backend files when working on frontend

questions.explanation: Custom Agents let teams version selectable role profiles. A frontend agent can declare browser tools and React instructions; another can declare the MCP servers and commands needed for backend work.

questions.text: What is the main difference between Custom Agents, Steering Files, and Skills in Kiro?

options.label: Steering and Skills are equivalent; Custom Agents only change the model used by chat

Steering provides persistent knowledge with inclusion modes; Skills package instructions and resources activated by relevance; Custom Agents define a selectable profile with prompt, tools, and permissions
Skills configure permissions; Steering installs MCP servers; Custom Agents store only reusable prompts
Custom Agents replace Steering and Skills, which stop loading when a specialized profile is selected

questions.explanation: Steering keeps project knowledge and can use `always`, `fileMatch`, `manual`, or `auto` inclusion. Skills are portable packages discovered and activated when a request matches their description. Custom Agents configure a selectable profile with a prompt, tools, MCP servers, and permissions.

questions.text: You want a specialized profile that users can select to review code against security standards using only authorized tools. Which approach is most appropriate?

options.label: Add security rules in the project's global steering file
Create a Custom Agent with a security-focused system prompt, configured in .kiro/agents/
Install a security linting extension in the editor
Create a `PostFileSave` Hook even though review should begin only when the user selects the profile

questions.explanation: A Custom Agent in `.kiro/agents/` can combine the review prompt, required tools, and permission rules. It is a selectable profile; if the requirement were automatic event-driven validation, Hooks would be the appropriate mechanism.
